title: Invertibility normalization for the canonical module-object projection
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring, f : X → Y a morphism of schemes, K an arbitrary object of D(Mod_{Λ_X}), and L an arbitrary object of D(Mod_{Λ_Y}). Use the specified derived adjunction Lf* ⊣ Rf* and its canonical monoidal structure [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. The canonical module-object projection map π_{f,K,L} [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map] is invertible if and only if the projection morphism of this monoidal adjunction is invertible. Both maps, their categories and endpoints are definitionally identical: the adjoint transpose of the oplax tensor comparison followed by counit tensor identity. No properness, boundedness, constructibility or coefficient-finiteness assumption is needed.

proof.text: Unfold the record projections defining moduleObjectProjectionMap and the adjunction projection morphism. Both use the same leftDerivedUpperStarTensor comparison, counit tensor identity, and adjunction hom equivalence, in the same category. Reflexivity proves the equivalence of their IsIso predicates, including the category and endpoints.

theorem isIso_moduleObjectProjectionMap_iff
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ Y))) :
    IsIso (moduleObjectProjectionMap Λ f K L) ↔
      IsIso ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction Λ f).projectionMorphism K L)
